title: Auto mode is now the default in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team plans
excerpt: Claude Code will soon run auto mode by default for Pro, Max, and Team plans, enabling longer-running autonomous work, and catching more dangerous commands.
content_html:
We're making auto mode the default in Claude Code. Starting on August 14, new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans will run in auto mode. If you've already set a different default yourself, you may get a one-time prompt asking whether you want to switch to auto mode. If you have a pinned default, nothing changes for you. The auto mode classifier uses a small number of extra tokens per tool call, and we're no longer charging Claude Code users on Pro, Max, and Team plans for that classifier overhead, effective today.

Auto mode remains opt-in for now on Claude Enterprise, the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry, giving admins time to review the change. In the coming month, working with our cloud partners, we plan to make it the default across all of these and no longer charge for classifier overhead. In the meantime, Enterprise admins can make Claude Code's auto mode the default through managed settings.

Auto mode is designed to balance users’ desire not to be interrupted with a system that helps avoid harmful actions: instead of prompts, it routes each tool call through a classifier targeted at blocking actions that are irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your environment. When the classifier blocks something, Claude usually finds a safer way to proceed on its own or asks you directly for the go-ahead; if it can't make progress—three blocks in a row, or twenty across a session—Claude Code falls back to manual approvals.

We spent the last several months testing whether auto mode is as safe or safer than an average user clicking through prompts. We ran internal red-teaming, third-party red-teaming and prompt-injection evaluations, a controlled study with 1,053 paid testers, and analysis of real production sessions. On every measure we tested, auto mode matched or outperformed manual review.

Auto mode also lets Claude work autonomously for longer stretches. This makes models built for long-running work, like Claude Opus 5, more practical to leave running for hours on large tasks. Reducing overhead for users also increases output. Among Teams & Enterprise adopters, auto mode users ship about 25% more PRs. Unblocking Claude allows tasks to run longer uninterrupted and get more work done. Teams at Adobe, Nuro, Gusto, and Garner Health already run auto mode as their production default. 

Below, we share the safety data and customer results motivating the change, and how to set a different default if you prefer.

Comparing manual review to auto mode

Data suggests that manual review can become habitual: users approve 97% of permission prompts in Claude Code. While most prompts are likely for safe, routine commands, an approval rate that high suggests many users are clicking through reflexively rather than reviewing each command. These prompts ask developers to make dozens or hundreds of important security decisions every day, often in the middle of projects, which places the review burden on users and increases the chance that something important slips through the cracks. Data also suggests that users more frequently scrutinize and push back on other types of dialogues: for example, when Claude presents a plan for approval, users reject 39% of them. But for individual permissions requests, the rejection rate is only 3%.

The same pattern shows up in settings files. As of June 2026, 49.5% of active CLI users have manually created a Bash allow-rule—5% allow any shell command outright, and another 43% have interpreter rules like Bash(python:*) or Bash(node:*) that are essentially equivalent in practice—and that share is growing roughly 5 percentage points every 5 weeks. Beyond allow-rules, 62% of users have used bypassPermissions or clicked “don't ask again” on Bash, and 25% of interactive sessions start in bypass permissions mode.

Permission rules still fire before the classifier in auto mode, except for allow rules broad enough to grant arbitrary code execution (e.g. python:*). These arbitrary rules are set aside while in auto mode, since they would let commands skip the classifier entirely. Settings files aren't modified, and the rules apply again the moment you switch to another mode.

Improving safety with auto mode

Research conducted internally and through several third parties suggests that auto mode is safer than how a typical user engages with permission prompts today. We tested auto mode against what developers actually approve when they're clicking through permission prompts. Across each of these measures—internal red-teaming, third-party penetration testing, and analysis of real-world sessions—auto mode matched or outperformed human approval.

Auto mode outperforms manual permissions on safety

We hired 1,053 paid testers through a research vendor for a coding study. These participants worked in a test environment set up specifically for the study, not in their own codebases or on real projects. Participants knew they were being evaluated, but—following standard blind-study design—weren't told which behavior was being measured. Partway through each session, a single permission prompt was swapped for a clearly dangerous command, and the vendor recorded whether the tester approved it (Note: approving the prompt never resulted in anything dangerous being run; only the text of the prompt testers saw was changed). 

The testers caught the dangerous command just 13.6% of the time (143 of 1,053), while auto mode blocked 89% of the same commands (937 of 1,053). Head to head, auto mode blocked 800 commands that a human approved, while humans blocked only 6 that auto mode allowed. As sessions got longer, humans did worse: they blocked about 17% of dangerous commands early in a session, dropping to about 5% after 50 or more prior prompts, while auto mode's block rate stayed flat regardless of session length.

Auto mode prevents more harmful actions

Our research also suggests that auto mode leads to fewer harmful actions than manual permissions mode.

We examined how auto mode performs in real usage. From May to June 2026, we examined sessions our safety pipeline had flagged for review, drawn only from accounts that have opted in to data use for training and analysis. We re-graded each one with a model on two 0–10 scales. The first was harm severity with 10 being company-wide, irreversible harm, such as leaking a company's entire source code, 7 representing production-level severity such as deleting rows from a production database, and 0 a fully reversible action confined to the local workspace, like overwriting a scratch file. The second was how explicitly the user had asked for the action, so we could separate harmful actions the user directly requested from harmful actions the agent took with less explicit direction.

Among the flagged sessions, those that went through manual approval contained serious unintended harm more than twice as often as auto mode sessions. At production-level severity (7+), 6.3% of manually approved sessions contained a harmful action the user hadn't explicitly asked for, compared to 2.4% of auto mode sessions, and the gap held at every severity level we tested. 

Adversarial red-teaming made auto mode stronger

We worked with Apollo Research, a UK-based AI safety startup, on a two-week pilot injecting synthetic attacks into real coding trajectories, across three datasets covering broad failures, data exfiltration, and safety-related threats.

The engagement followed a standard find-fix-verify loop. Apollo shared a set of successful attacks along with recommendations to strengthen auto mode. We hardened the classifier against them primarily by giving it more context about the environment it's protecting (repository visibility, git state, and the data-handling rules described below).

After hardening, Apollo re-tested on a separate held-out attack set that we never had access to. Auto mode caught about half of the attacks it previously missed, at a cost of missing about 2% of attacks it previously caught. Since we couldn't tune against the held-out set, this suggests the hardening generalizes to new attacks rather than patching the specific ones Apollo shared. Across both the shared and held-out sets, the classifier's miss rate fell from 12% to 7%.

These attacks are synthetic and adversarial by design, built to find where the classifier fails, and more malicious than anything Claude would do unprompted. The 7% miss rate is measured against this set and should not be taken as the miss rate on real traffic.

Auto mode reduces prompt injection risk

The auto mode classifier adds an additional layer of defense against prompt injection attacks that try to force the agent to deviate from the user’s instructions. When running with auto mode, tool results are scanned by probes for potentially malicious instructions, and auto mode checks that actions are aligned with user intent. We tested auto mode compared to an unguarded model to illustrate the power of this defense-in-depth approach.

We commissioned an evaluation from a third party, Trajectory Labs, who tested different models within the latest publicly available versions of Claude Code and Codex as of July 17th 2026.1 They tested 72 indirect prompt injection scenarios held out from Anthropic. Each scenario was tested 10 times. Successful attacks would, in a non-testing environment, result in irreversible actions that could harm the user such as sensitive-data exfiltration, financial fraud, or credential phishing. The attacks were optimized against Claude Opus 4.7, which is not in the reported set, so every model in the evaluation faced them as unseen attacks. In addition to auto mode, the evaluations looked at Claude Code’s bypassPermissions mode and Codex’s Full Access mode.

Both Codex and Claude Code were evaluated using an identical browser integration produced by Trajectory Labs, PBC. This integration provides a set of MCP tools which are a thin wrapper around common Chrome APIs such as `navigate`. Safeguards built into first-party browser integrations such as the Chrome extensions provided by OpenAI and Anthropic were not tested. As such, these results should be viewed as a measurement of the underlying model, rather than the complete set of safeguards which might exist in a given deployment.

In this evaluation, none of the 720 attack attempts succeeded against Claude Fable 5, Opus 5, or Sonnet 5 running auto mode. On the other hand, 5.83% of the attacks succeeded against GPT-5.6 Sol running Codex's Auto-review mode. Notably, this is greater than the 0.09% average attack success rate against our latest models running in bypassPermissions mode without additional safeguards. The tests showed a 19.03% attack success rate against GPT-5.6 Sol when running in Full Access mode. Attack success rates differ between tasks where tools return results as text and tasks that require interacting with a browser through screenshots, as shown below.

Three incidents auto mode prevented inside Anthropic

Auto mode is also the default for all Claude Code internal usage at Anthropic. Here are three actions the classifier prevented internally:

  • An off-network data leak: When an upload to an internal drive failed, Claude's fallback was to publish the same report to a public code-sharing site. Auto mode denied the fallback and prompted the user for next steps.
  • A destructive mass operation: In a long-running session, Claude attempted a mass process kill across roughly two thousand pods and queued deletions that would have torn down hundreds of GPUs of in-flight training jobs. Auto mode flagged the destructive commands before execution.
  • Over-broad privilege escalation: Asked to provision read-only billing access, Claude reached for a cloud role that grants full administrative control at the account root. Auto mode caught the mismatch between what was requested and what roles would have been granted.

In each case, Claude either found a safer path on its own or checked in with the user before proceeding.

Making auto mode even safer 

We’re continuously investing in new auto mode features that make it safer and easier to ship production code. Recent examples include: 

  • Hard denies: Data exfiltration, like sending your code or secrets somewhere external, sits in a category the classifier is designed to never approve. To run an action like that, you have to switch out of auto mode or run the command yourself. Hard deny rules are customizable via settings so you can add more rules that you never want allowed even when requested by users in your organization.
  • Rules for data access and sharing: The classifier now carries explicit rules distinguishing secrets and potentially sensitive/confidential information—and where each can be accessed and shared. To make those rules enforceable, it also checks whether the destination of a git push or pull request is public, private, or trusted before the action runs. The same push can be routine or an exfiltration depending on where it lands: code that belongs in your team's private repository shouldn't end up in a public one, and the classifier is now designed to flag when this might happen.
  • Checking git status before destructive git actions: Before a command that could discard uncommitted work, like git reset --hard, the classifier sees the repository's current git status, letting auto mode know what is being reset.
  • Prompt injection screening: When Claude pulls content from external sources, like web pages, file contents, or tool outputs, an API-side probe checks that content for attempts to hijack Claude's behavior. When something looks like an injection attempt, a warning is added to Claude's context before the result is shared with the user.

Auto mode in production 

Teams are already running auto mode as their production default:

  • Adobe's merchandising platform team is responsible for keeping pricing and promotional pages accurate and current across 90+ countries and 30+ languages on Adobe.com. They built an agentic loop to build and verify those pages, running it in auto mode so engineers receive finished PRs for review. 
  • Nuro runs auto mode across its research and engineering orgs, using it to power overnight research agents that hill-climb evaluation metrics and return finished PRs for review by morning.
  • Gusto adopted auto mode to end the permission fatigue that was pushing engineers toward bypassing permissions checks entirely. About 10% of sessions since mid-May include a classifier denial—evidence it's doing real work without slowing legitimate tasks.
  • Garner Health pushed auto mode as the default to all 550 employees via managed settings, standardizing a company-wide software development lifecycle (SDLC) that no longer depends on hand-curated command allowlists.

Learn how these customers are running auto mode in production. 

Getting started

For Pro, Max, and Team users: if you haven’t set a default permission mode, you’ll receive an in-product notice and new sessions will start in auto mode automatically. If you've set a different default, you may see a one-time prompt asking if you’d like to switch your default to auto mode. If your Team admin has set a default in managed settings, nothing changes for you.

For Enterprise users and users who access Claude Code via the Claude API, auto mode remains opt-in for now. We plan to make auto mode the default in the coming month, and we’ll notify Enterprise admins before we do.

To switch modes, press Shift+Tab in the CLI or use the mode dropdown on the desktop app. Admins can pin an org-wide default with `defaultMode` in managed settings, or turn auto mode off entirely with `disableAutoMode`.

Finally, while we believe auto mode reduces risk for most users, it relies on classification systems and therefore does not eliminate risk. For high-stakes changes to production infrastructure, we still recommend reviewing Claude's actions yourself. See the auto mode docs for full configuration instructions.

blocks.html_en: Auto mode is designed to balance users’ desire not to be interrupted with a system that helps avoid harmful actions: instead of prompts, it routes each tool call through a classifier targeted at blocking actions that are irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your environment. When the classifier blocks something, Claude usually finds a safer way to proceed on its own or asks you directly for the go-ahead; if it can't make progress—three blocks in a row, or twenty across a session—Claude Code falls back to manual approvals.

We ran internal red-teaming, third-party red-teaming and prompt-injection evaluations, a controlled study with 1,053 paid testers, and analysis of real production sessions. On every measure we tested, auto mode matched or outperformed manual review.

blocks.html_en: Comparing manual review to auto mode

sentences.en: Comparing manual review to auto mode
sentences.zh: 手动审核与自动模式的比较

blocks.html_en: Data suggests that manual review can become habitual: users approve 97% of permission prompts in Claude Code. While most prompts are likely for safe, routine commands, an approval rate that high suggests many users are clicking through reflexively rather than reviewing each command. These prompts ask developers to make dozens or hundreds of important security decisions every day, often in the middle of projects, which places the review burden on users and increases the chance that something important slips through the cracks. Data also suggests that users more frequently scrutinize and push back on other types of dialogues: for example, when Claude presents a plan for approval, users reject 39% of them. But for individual permissions requests, the rejection rate is only 3%.

blocks.html_en: The same pattern shows up in settings files. As of June 2026, 49.5% of active CLI users have manually created a Bash allow-rule—5% allow any shell command outright, and another 43% have interpreter rules like Bash(python:*) or Bash(node:*) that are essentially equivalent in practice—and that share is growing roughly 5 percentage points every 5 weeks. Beyond allow-rules, 62% of users have used bypassPermissions or clicked “don't ask again” on Bash, and 25% of interactive sessions start in bypass permissions mode.

blocks.html_en: Improving safety with auto mode

sentences.en: Improving safety with auto mode
sentences.zh: 通过自动模式提高安全性

blocks.html_en: Research conducted internally and through several third parties suggests that auto mode is safer than how a typical user engages with permission prompts today. We tested auto mode against what developers actually approve when they're clicking through permission prompts. Across each of these measures—internal red-teaming, third-party penetration testing, and analysis of real-world sessions—auto mode matched or outperformed human approval.

sentences.en: Research conducted internally and through several third parties suggests that auto mode is safer than how a typical user engages with permission prompts today.
sentences.zh: 内部和通过多个第三方进行的研究表明，自动模式比当今典型用户处理权限提示的方式更安全。

sentences.en: We tested auto mode against what developers actually approve when they're clicking through permission prompts.
sentences.zh: 我们根据开发人员在单击权限提示时实际批准的内容测试了自动模式。

sentences.en: Across each of these measures—internal red-teaming, third-party penetration testing, and analysis of real-world sessions—auto mode matched or outperformed human approval.
sentences.zh: 在每一项措施（内部红队、第三方渗透测试和现实世界会话分析）中，自动模式都匹配或优于人类批准。

blocks.html_en: Auto mode outperforms manual permissions on safety

sentences.en: Auto mode outperforms manual permissions on safety
sentences.zh: 自动模式在安全性方面优于手动权限

sentences.en: In a controlled experiment with 1,053 paid professional testers, human review caught just 13.6% of dangerous commands, while auto mode caught 89%.
sentences.zh: 在一项由 1,053 名付费专业测试人员参与的对照实验中，人工审查仅捕获了 13.6% 的危险命令，而自动模式捕获了 89%。

blocks.html_en: We hired 1,053 paid testers through a research vendor for a coding study. These participants worked in a test environment set up specifically for the study, not in their own codebases or on real projects. Participants knew they were being evaluated, but—following standard blind-study design—weren't told which behavior was being measured. Partway through each session, a single permission prompt was swapped for a clearly dangerous command, and the vendor recorded whether the tester approved it (Note: approving the prompt never resulted in anything dangerous being run; only the text of the prompt testers saw was changed).

sentences.en: We hired 1,053 paid testers through a research vendor for a coding study.
sentences.zh: 我们通过研究供应商聘请了 1,053 名付费测试人员进行编码研究。

sentences.en: These participants worked in a test environment set up specifically for the study, not in their own codebases or on real projects.
sentences.zh: 这些参与者在专门为研究设置的测试环境中工作，而不是在他们自己的代码库或实际项目中工作。

sentences.en: Participants knew they were being evaluated, but—following standard blind-study design—weren't told which behavior was being measured.
sentences.zh: 参与者知道他们正在接受评估，但是按照标准的盲目研究设计，他们不知道正在评估哪些行为。

sentences.en: Partway through each session, a single permission prompt was swapped for a clearly dangerous command, and the vendor recorded whether the tester approved it (Note: approving the prompt never resulted in anything dangerous being run; only the text of the prompt testers saw was changed).
sentences.zh: 在每个会话的中途，单个权限提示被替换为明显危险的命令，供应商记录测试人员是否批准它（注意：批准提示永远不会导致任何危险的运行；只有测试人员看到的提示文本发生了变化）。

blocks.html_en: The testers caught the dangerous command just 13.6% of the time (143 of 1,053), while auto mode blocked 89% of the same commands (937 of 1,053). Head to head, auto mode blocked 800 commands that a human approved, while humans blocked only 6 that auto mode allowed. As sessions got longer, humans did worse: they blocked about 17% of dangerous commands early in a session, dropping to about 5% after 50 or more prior prompts, while auto mode's block rate stayed flat regardless of session length.

sentences.en: The testers caught the dangerous command just 13.6% of the time (143 of 1,053), while auto mode blocked 89% of the same commands (937 of 1,053).
sentences.zh: 测试人员仅在 13.6% 的时间内捕获了危险命令（1,053 次中的 143 次），而自动模式则阻止了 89% 的相同命令（1,053 次中的 937 次）。

sentences.en: Head to head, auto mode blocked 800 commands that a human approved, while humans blocked only 6 that auto mode allowed.
sentences.zh: 对比之下，自动模式阻止了人类批准的 800 个命令，而人类只阻止了自动模式允许的 6 个命令。

sentences.en: As sessions got longer, humans did worse: they blocked about 17% of dangerous commands early in a session, dropping to about 5% after 50 or more prior prompts, while auto mode's block rate stayed flat regardless of session length.
sentences.zh: 随着会话时间的延长，人类的表现变得更糟：他们在会话早期阻止了大约 17% 的危险命令，在 50 个或更多先前提示后下降到大约 5%，而无论会话长度如何，自动模式的阻止率都保持不变。

blocks.html_en: Auto mode prevents more harmful actions

sentences.en: Auto mode prevents more harmful actions
sentences.zh: 自动模式可防止更多有害行为

blocks.html_en: Our research also suggests that auto mode leads to fewer harmful actions than manual permissions mode.

sentences.en: Our research also suggests that auto mode leads to fewer harmful actions than manual permissions mode.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究还表明，自动模式比手动权限模式导致的有害操作更少。

blocks.html_en: We examined how auto mode performs in real usage. From May to June 2026, we examined sessions our safety pipeline had flagged for review, drawn only from accounts that have opted in to data use for training and analysis. We re-graded each one with a model on two 0–10 scales. The first was harm severity with 10 being company-wide, irreversible harm, such as leaking a company's entire source code, 7 representing production-level severity such as deleting rows from a production database, and 0 a fully reversible action confined to the local workspace, like overwriting a scratch file. The second was how explicitly the user had asked for the action, so we could separate harmful actions the user directly requested from harmful actions the agent took with less explicit direction.

sentences.en: We examined how auto mode performs in real usage.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了自动模式在实际使用中的表现。

sentences.en: From May to June 2026, we examined sessions our safety pipeline had flagged for review, drawn only from accounts that have opted in to data use for training and analysis.
sentences.zh: 从 2026 年 5 月到 2026 年 6 月，我们检查了安全管道标记为需要审查的会话，这些会话仅来自选择使用数据进行培训和分析的账户。

sentences.en: We re-graded each one with a model on two 0–10 scales.
sentences.zh: 我们用两个 0-10 等级的模型对每个模型进行了重新评分。

sentences.en: The first was harm severity with 10 being company-wide, irreversible harm, such as leaking a company's entire source code, 7 representing production-level severity such as deleting rows from a production database, and 0 a fully reversible action confined to the local workspace, like overwriting a scratch file.
sentences.zh: 第一个是危害严重程度，10 表示公司范围内的不可逆转的危害，例如泄露公司的整个源代码，7 表示生产级严重程度，例如从生产数据库中删除行，0 表示仅限于本地工作区的完全可逆操作，例如覆盖临时文件。

sentences.en: The second was how explicitly the user had asked for the action, so we could separate harmful actions the user directly requested from harmful actions the agent took with less explicit direction.
sentences.zh: 第二个是用户请求操作的明确程度，因此我们可以将用户直接请求的有害操作与代理在不太明确的指示下采取的有害操作分开。

blocks.html_en: Among the flagged sessions, those that went through manual approval contained serious unintended harm more than twice as often as auto mode sessions. At production-level severity (7+), 6.3% of manually approved sessions contained a harmful action the user hadn't explicitly asked for, compared to 2.4% of auto mode sessions, and the gap held at every severity level we tested.

sentences.en: Among the flagged sessions, those that went through manual approval contained serious unintended harm more than twice as often as auto mode sessions.
sentences.zh: 在标记的会话中，经过手动批准的会话所造成的严重意外伤害是自动模式会话的两倍多。

sentences.en: At production-level severity (7+), 6.3% of manually approved sessions contained a harmful action the user hadn't explicitly asked for, compared to 2.4% of auto mode sessions, and the gap held at every severity level we tested.
sentences.zh: 在生产级别严重性 (7+) 下，6.3% 的手动批准会话包含用户未明确要求的有害操作，而自动模式会话中这一比例为 2.4%，并且在我们测试的每个严重性级别上都存在差距。

blocks.html_en: Adversarial red-teaming made auto mode stronger

sentences.en: Adversarial red-teaming made auto mode stronger
sentences.zh: 对抗性红队让自动模式变得更强

blocks.html_en: We worked with Apollo Research, a UK-based AI safety startup, on a two-week pilot injecting synthetic attacks into real coding trajectories, across three datasets covering broad failures, data exfiltration, and safety-related threats.

sentences.en: We worked with Apollo Research, a UK-based AI safety startup, on a two-week pilot injecting synthetic attacks into real coding trajectories, across three datasets covering broad failures, data exfiltration, and safety-related threats.
sentences.zh: 我们与总部位于英国的人工智能安全初创公司 Apollo Research 合作，进行了为期两周的试点，将合成攻击注入到真实的编码轨迹中，涉及三个数据集，涵盖广泛的故障、数据泄露和安全相关威胁。

blocks.html_en: The engagement followed a standard find-fix-verify loop. Apollo shared a set of successful attacks along with recommendations to strengthen auto mode. We hardened the classifier against them primarily by giving it more context about the environment it's protecting (repository visibility, git state, and the data-handling rules described below).

sentences.en: The engagement followed a standard find-fix-verify loop.
sentences.zh: 参与遵循标准的查找-修复-验证循环。

sentences.en: Apollo shared a set of successful attacks along with recommendations to strengthen auto mode.
sentences.zh: Apollo 分享了一系列成功的攻击以及加强自动模式的建议。

sentences.en: We hardened the classifier against them primarily by giving it more context about the environment it's protecting (repository visibility, git state, and the data-handling rules described below).
sentences.zh: 我们主要通过为分类器提供更多有关其所保护的环境的背景信息（存储库可见性、git 状态和下面描述的数据处理规则）来强化分类器。

blocks.html_en: After hardening, Apollo re-tested on a separate held-out attack set that we never had access to. Auto mode caught about half of the attacks it previously missed, at a cost of missing about 2% of attacks it previously caught. Since we couldn't tune against the held-out set, this suggests the hardening generalizes to new attacks rather than patching the specific ones Apollo shared. Across both the shared and held-out sets, the classifier's miss rate fell from 12% to 7%.

sentences.en: After hardening, Apollo re-tested on a separate held-out attack set that we never had access to.
sentences.zh: 强化后，阿波罗在我们从未访问过的单独的保留攻击集上重新进行了测试。

sentences.en: Auto mode caught about half of the attacks it previously missed, at a cost of missing about 2% of attacks it previously caught.
sentences.zh: 自动模式捕获了之前错过的大约一半的攻击，代价是错过了之前捕获的大约 2% 的攻击。

sentences.en: Since we couldn't tune against the held-out set, this suggests the hardening generalizes to new attacks rather than patching the specific ones Apollo shared.
sentences.zh: 由于我们无法针对保留的集合进行调整，这表明强化适用于新的攻击，而不是修补 Apollo 共享的特定攻击。

sentences.en: Across both the shared and held-out sets, the classifier's miss rate fell from 12% to 7%.
sentences.zh: 在共享集和保留集上，分类器的漏失率从 12% 下降到 7%。

blocks.html_en: These attacks are synthetic and adversarial by design, built to find where the classifier fails, and more malicious than anything Claude would do unprompted. The 7% miss rate is measured against this set and should not be taken as the miss rate on real traffic.

sentences.en: These attacks are synthetic and adversarial by design, built to find where the classifier fails, and more malicious than anything Claude would do unprompted.
sentences.zh: 这些攻击是综合性的、对抗性的，是为了找出分类器失败的地方而设计的，而且比克劳德在没有提示的情况下所做的任何攻击都更加恶意。

sentences.en: The 7% miss rate is measured against this set and should not be taken as the miss rate on real traffic.
sentences.zh: 7% 的丢失率是针对该集合进行测量的，不应将其视为实际流量的丢失率。

blocks.html_en: Auto mode reduces prompt injection risk

sentences.en: Auto mode reduces prompt injection risk
sentences.zh: 自动模式降低即时注入风险

sentences.en: With auto mode enabled, no attack in an independent evaluation was successful against any of our models.
sentences.zh: 启用自动模式后，在独立评估中，针对我们的任何模型的攻击均未成功。

sentences.en: GPT-5.6 Sol running in Codex v0.144.5 Auto-review permission mode had a 5.83% attack success rate.
sentences.zh: 在 Codex v0.144.5 自动审查权限模式下运行的 GPT-5.6 Sol 的攻击成功率为 5.83%。

sentences.en: GPT-5.6 Sol was run on “max” reasoning effort to test performance with its highest level of reasoning, and all Claude models were run on high effort.
sentences.zh: GPT-5.6 Sol 以“最大”推理努力运行，以测试最高推理水平的性能，并且所有 Claude 模型都以高努力运行。

blocks.html_en: The auto mode classifier adds an additional layer of defense against prompt injection attacks that try to force the agent to deviate from the user’s instructions. When running with auto mode, tool results are scanned by probes for potentially malicious instructions, and auto mode checks that actions are aligned with user intent. We tested auto mode compared to an unguarded model to illustrate the power of this defense-in-depth approach.

sentences.en: The auto mode classifier adds an additional layer of defense against prompt injection attacks that try to force the agent to deviate from the user’s instructions.
sentences.zh: 自动模式分类器增加了一层额外的防御，以防止提示注入攻击试图迫使代理偏离用户的指令。

sentences.en: When running with auto mode, tool results are scanned by probes for potentially malicious instructions, and auto mode checks that actions are aligned with user intent.
sentences.zh: 在自动模式下运行时，探针会扫描工具结果以查找潜在的恶意指令，并且自动模式会检查操作是否与用户意图一致。

sentences.en: We tested auto mode compared to an unguarded model to illustrate the power of this defense-in-depth approach.
sentences.zh: 我们测试了自动模式与无防护模式的比较，以说明这种纵深防御方法的强大功能。

blocks.html_en: We commissioned an evaluation from a third party, Trajectory Labs, who tested different models within the latest publicly available versions of Claude Code and Codex as of July 17th 2026.1 They tested 72 indirect prompt injection scenarios held out from Anthropic. Each scenario was tested 10 times. Successful attacks would, in a non-testing environment, result in irreversible actions that could harm the user such as sensitive-data exfiltration, financial fraud, or credential phishing. The attacks were optimized against Claude Opus 4.7, which is not in the reported set, so every model in the evaluation faced them as unseen attacks. In addition to auto mode, the evaluations looked at Claude Code’s bypassPermissions mode and Codex’s Full Access mode.

blocks.html_en: Both Codex and Claude Code were evaluated using an identical browser integration produced by Trajectory Labs, PBC. This integration provides a set of MCP tools which are a thin wrapper around common Chrome APIs such as `navigate`. Safeguards built into first-party browser integrations such as the Chrome extensions provided by OpenAI and Anthropic were not tested. As such, these results should be viewed as a measurement of the underlying model, rather than the complete set of safeguards which might exist in a given deployment.

blocks.html_en: Three incidents auto mode prevented inside Anthropic

sentences.en: Three incidents auto mode prevented inside Anthropic
sentences.zh: Anthropic 内部避免了三起自动模式事故

blocks.html_en: Auto mode is also the default for all Claude Code internal usage at Anthropic. Here are three actions the classifier prevented internally:

sentences.en: Auto mode is also the default for all Claude Code internal usage at Anthropic.
sentences.zh: 自动模式也是 Anthropic 所有 Claude Code 内部使用的默认模式。

sentences.en: Here are three actions the classifier prevented internally:
sentences.zh: 以下是分类器在内部阻止的三个操作：

blocks.html_en: • An off-network data leak: When an upload to an internal drive failed, Claude's fallback was to publish the same report to a public code-sharing site. Auto mode denied the fallback and prompted the user for next steps.

sentences.en: An off-network data leak: When an upload to an internal drive failed, Claude's fallback was to publish the same report to a public code-sharing site.
sentences.zh: 网外数据泄露：当上传到内部驱动器失败时，克劳德的后备措施是将相同的报告发布到公共代码共享网站。

sentences.en: Auto mode denied the fallback and prompted the user for next steps.
sentences.zh: 自动模式拒绝回退并提示用户执行后续步骤。

blocks.html_en: • A destructive mass operation: In a long-running session, Claude attempted a mass process kill across roughly two thousand pods and queued deletions that would have torn down hundreds of GPUs of in-flight training jobs. Auto mode flagged the destructive commands before execution.

sentences.en: A destructive mass operation: In a long-running session, Claude attempted a mass process kill across roughly two thousand pods and queued deletions that would have torn down hundreds of GPUs of in-flight training jobs.
sentences.zh: 破坏性的大规模操作：在一次长时间运行的会话中，Claude 尝试对大约 2000 个 Pod 进行大规模进程终止，并进行排队删除，这可能会导致数百个正在运行的训练作业的 GPU 崩溃。

sentences.en: Auto mode flagged the destructive commands before execution.
sentences.zh: 自动模式在执行前标记破坏性命令。

blocks.html_en: • Over-broad privilege escalation: Asked to provision read-only billing access, Claude reached for a cloud role that grants full administrative control at the account root. Auto mode caught the mismatch between what was requested and what roles would have been granted.

sentences.en: Over-broad privilege escalation: Asked to provision read-only billing access, Claude reached for a cloud role that grants full administrative control at the account root.
sentences.zh: 过于广泛的权限升级：当要求提供只读计费访问权限时，Claude 找到了一个云角色，可以在帐户根目录授予完全的管理控制权。

sentences.en: Auto mode caught the mismatch between what was requested and what roles would have been granted.
sentences.zh: 自动模式发现了请求的内容与授予的角色之间的不匹配。

blocks.html_en: In each case, Claude either found a safer path on its own or checked in with the user before proceeding.

sentences.en: In each case, Claude either found a safer path on its own or checked in with the user before proceeding.
sentences.zh: 在每种情况下，克劳德要么自己找到一条更安全的路径，要么在继续之前与用户核实。

blocks.html_en: Making auto mode even safer

sentences.en: Making auto mode even safer
sentences.zh: 让自动模式更安全

blocks.html_en: We’re continuously investing in new auto mode features that make it safer and easier to ship production code. Recent examples include:

sentences.en: We’re continuously investing in new auto mode features that make it safer and easier to ship production code.
sentences.zh: 我们不断投资新的自动模式功能，使交付生产代码更安全、更轻松。

sentences.en: Recent examples include:
sentences.zh: 最近的例子包括：

blocks.html_en: • Hard denies: Data exfiltration, like sending your code or secrets somewhere external, sits in a category the classifier is designed to never approve. To run an action like that, you have to switch out of auto mode or run the command yourself. Hard deny rules are customizable via settings so you can add more rules that you never want allowed even when requested by users in your organization.

sentences.en: Hard denies: Data exfiltration, like sending your code or secrets somewhere external, sits in a category the classifier is designed to never approve.
sentences.zh: 硬否认：数据泄露，例如将您的代码或秘密发送到外部某个地方，属于分类器设计永远不会批准的类别。

sentences.en: To run an action like that, you have to switch out of auto mode or run the command yourself.
sentences.zh: 要运行这样的操作，您必须退出自动模式或自己运行命令。

sentences.en: Hard deny rules are customizable via settings so you can add more rules that you never want allowed even when requested by users in your organization.
sentences.zh: 硬拒绝规则可通过设置进行自定义，因此您可以添加更多您永远不想允许的规则，即使组织中的用户请求也是如此。

blocks.html_en: • Rules for data access and sharing: The classifier now carries explicit rules distinguishing secrets and potentially sensitive/confidential information—and where each can be accessed and shared. To make those rules enforceable, it also checks whether the destination of a git push or pull request is public, private, or trusted before the action runs. The same push can be routine or an exfiltration depending on where it lands: code that belongs in your team's private repository shouldn't end up in a public one, and the classifier is now designed to flag when this might happen.

sentences.en: Rules for data access and sharing: The classifier now carries explicit rules distinguishing secrets and potentially sensitive/confidential information—and where each can be accessed and shared.
sentences.zh: 数据访问和共享规则：分类器现在带有区分秘密和潜在敏感/机密信息的明确规则，以及每个信息可以访问和共享的位置。

sentences.en: To make those rules enforceable, it also checks whether the destination of a git push or pull request is public, private, or trusted before the action runs.
sentences.zh: 为了使这些规则可执行，它还会在操作运行之前检查 git Push 或 Pull 请求的目的地是公共的、私有的还是受信任的。

sentences.en: The same push can be routine or an exfiltration depending on where it lands: code that belongs in your team's private repository shouldn't end up in a public one, and the classifier is now designed to flag when this might happen.
sentences.zh: 同样的推送可以是例行公事，也可以是渗透，具体取决于它所在的位置：属于团队私有存储库中的代码不应最终出现在公共存储库中，并且分类器现在旨在标记何时可能发生这种情况。

blocks.html_en: • Checking git status before destructive git actions: Before a command that could discard uncommitted work, like git reset --hard, the classifier sees the repository's current git status, letting auto mode know what is being reset.

sentences.en: Checking git status before destructive git actions: Before a command that could discard uncommitted work, like git reset --hard, the classifier sees the repository's current git status, letting auto mode know what is being reset.
sentences.zh: 在破坏性 git 操作之前检查 git 状态：在可能丢弃未提交工作的命令（例如 git reset --hard）之前，分类器会查看存储库的当前 git 状态，让自动模式知道正在重置的内容。

blocks.html_en: • Prompt injection screening: When Claude pulls content from external sources, like web pages, file contents, or tool outputs, an API-side probe checks that content for attempts to hijack Claude's behavior. When something looks like an injection attempt, a warning is added to Claude's context before the result is shared with the user.

sentences.en: Prompt injection screening: When Claude pulls content from external sources, like web pages, file contents, or tool outputs, an API-side probe checks that content for attempts to hijack Claude's behavior.
sentences.zh: 提示注入筛选：当 Claude 从外部来源（例如网页、文件内容或工具输出）提取内容时，API 端探测器会检查该内容是否试图劫持 Claude 的行为。

content_html_zh:
我们将自动模式设为 Claude Code 中的默认模式。 从 8 月 14 日开始，Pro、Max 和 Team 计划的新会话将以自动模式运行。 如果您自己已经设置了不同的默认值，您可能会收到一次性提示，询问您是否要切换到自动模式。 如果您有固定的默认值，则不会发生任何变化。 自动模式分类器每次工具调用都会使用少量额外令牌，并且我们不再向 Pro、Max 和 Team 计划的 Claude Code 用户收取该分类器开销，从今天开始生效。

目前，Claude Enterprise、Claude API、AWS 上的 Claude Platform、Amazon Bedrock、Google Cloud 代理平台和 Microsoft Foundry 仍可选择自动模式，让管理员有时间审查更改。 在接下来的一个月里，我们与我们的云合作伙伴合作，计划将其设为所有这些的默认设置，并且不再收取分类器开销。 同时，企业管理员可以通过托管设置将 Claude Code 的自动模式设置为默认模式。

自动模式旨在平衡用户不被打扰的愿望，系统有助于避免有害操作：它不是提示，而是通过分类器路由每个工具调用，旨在阻止不可逆、破坏性或针对环境之外的操作。 当分类器阻止某件事时，克劳德通常会找到一种更安全的方式自行继续或直接请求您批准；如果无法取得进展（连续三个区块，或者一次会话中的二十个区块），克劳德·科德（Claude Code）就会退回到手动批准。

我们在过去的几个月里测试了自动模式是否与普通用户点击提示一样安全或更安全。 我们进行了内部红队、第三方红队和即时注入评估、对 1,053 名付费测试人员进行的对照研究以及对实际生产会话的分析。 在我们测试的每项指标中，自动模式均匹配或优于手动审核。

自动模式还可以让克劳德自主工作更长的时间。 这使得为​​长时间运行的工作构建的模型（例如 Claude Opus 5）更适合在大型任务上运行数小时。 减少用户的开销也会增加产出。 在 Teams 和 Enterprise 采用者中，自动模式用户发送的 PR 增加了约 25%。 解锁克劳德可以让任务不间断地运行更长时间并完成更多工作。 Adobe、Nuro、Gusto 和 Garner Health 的团队已将自动模式作为其生产默认设置。

下面，我们分享了推动变革的安全数据和客户结果，以及如何设置不同的默认值（如果您愿意）。

手动审核与自动模式的比较

数据表明，手动审核可能会成为习惯：用户批准 Claude Code 中 97% 的权限提示。 虽然大多数提示可能都是安全的常规命令，但如此高的批准率表明许多用户会条件反射地点击而不是查看每个命令。 这些提示要求开发人员每天（通常是在项目中间）做出数十或数百个重要的安全决策，这给用户带来了审查负担，并增加了重要内容被遗漏的机会。 数据还表明，用户更频繁地审查和抵制其他类型的对话：例如，当克劳德提出一项计划供批准时，用户拒绝其中的 39%。 但对于个人权限请求，拒绝率仅为 3%。

设置文件中也显示相同的模式。 截至 2026 年 6 月，49.5% 的活跃 CLI 用户手动创建了 Bash 允许规则——5% 完全允许任何 shell 命令，另外 43% 的用户拥有 Bash(python:*) 或 Bash(node:*) 之类的解释器规则，这些规则在实践中基本上是等效的——并且该比例每 5 周增长大约 5 个百分点。 除了允许规则之外，62% 的用户在 Bash 上使用了bypassPermissions 或单击了“不再询问”，并且 25% 的交互式会话以绕过权限模式启动。

在自动模式下，权限规则仍然在分类器之前触发，但允许规则足够广泛以授予任意代码执行（例如 python:*）。 这些任意规则在自动模式下被搁置，因为它们会让命令完全跳过分类器。 设置文件不会被修改，并且当您切换到另一种模式时，规则会再次应用。

通过自动模式提高安全性

内部和通过多个第三方进行的研究表明，自动模式比当今典型用户处理权限提示的方式更安全。 我们根据开发人员在单击权限提示时实际批准的内容测试了自动模式。 在每一项措施（内部红队、第三方渗透测试和现实世界会话分析）中，自动模式都匹配或优于人类批准。

自动模式在安全性方面优于手动权限

我们通过研究供应商聘请了 1,053 名付费测试人员进行编码研究。 这些参与者在专门为研究设置的测试环境中工作，而不是在他们自己的代码库或实际项目中工作。 参与者知道他们正在接受评估，但是按照标准的盲目研究设计，他们不知道正在评估哪些行为。 在每个会话的中途，单个权限提示被替换为明显危险的命令，供应商记录测试人员是否批准它（注意：批准提示永远不会导致任何危险的运行；只有测试人员看到的提示文本发生了变化）。

测试人员仅在 13.6% 的时间内捕获了危险命令（1,053 次中的 143 次），而自动模式则阻止了 89% 的相同命令（1,053 次中的 937 次）。 对比之下，自动模式阻止了人类批准的 800 个命令，而人类只阻止了自动模式允许的 6 个命令。 随着会话时间的延长，人类的表现变得更糟：他们在会话早期阻止了大约 17% 的危险命令，在 50 个或更多先前提示后下降到大约 5%，而无论会话长度如何，自动模式的阻止率都保持不变。

自动模式可防止更多有害行为

我们的研究还表明，自动模式比手动权限模式导致的有害操作更少。

我们研究了自动模式在实际使用中的表现。 从 2026 年 5 月到 2026 年 6 月，我们检查了安全管道标记为需要审查的会话，这些会话仅来自选择使用数据进行培训和分析的账户。 我们用两个 0-10 等级的模型对每个模型进行了重新评分。 第一个是危害严重程度，10 表示公司范围内的不可逆转的危害，例如泄露公司的整个源代码，7 表示生产级严重程度，例如从生产数据库中删除行，0 表示仅限于本地工作区的完全可逆操作，例如覆盖临时文件。 第二个是用户请求操作的明确程度，因此我们可以将用户直接请求的有害操作与代理在不太明确的指示下采取的有害操作分开。

在标记的会话中，经过手动批准的会话所造成的严重意外伤害是自动模式会话的两倍多。 在生产级别严重性 (7+) 下，6.3% 的手动批准会话包含用户未明确要求的有害操作，而自动模式会话中这一比例为 2.4%，并且在我们测试的每个严重性级别上都存在差距。

对抗性红队让自动模式变得更强

我们与总部位于英国的人工智能安全初创公司 Apollo Research 合作，进行了为期两周的试点，将合成攻击注入到真实的编码轨迹中，涉及三个数据集，涵盖广泛的故障、数据泄露和安全相关威胁。

参与遵循标准的查找-修复-验证循环。 Apollo 分享了一系列成功的攻击以及加强自动模式的建议。 我们主要通过为分类器提供更多有关其所保护的环境的背景信息（存储库可见性、git 状态和下面描述的数据处理规则）来强化分类器。

强化后，阿波罗在我们从未访问过的单独的保留攻击集上重新进行了测试。 自动模式捕获了之前错过的大约一半的攻击，代价是错过了之前捕获的大约 2% 的攻击。 由于我们无法针对保留的集合进行调整，这表明强化适用于新的攻击，而不是修补 Apollo 共享的特定攻击。 在共享集和保留集上，分类器的漏失率从 12% 下降到 7%。

这些攻击是综合性的、对抗性的，是为了找出分类器失败的地方而设计的，而且比克劳德在没有提示的情况下所做的任何攻击都更加恶意。 7% 的丢失率是针对该集合进行测量的，不应将其视为实际流量的丢失率。

自动模式降低即时注入风险

自动模式分类器增加了一层额外的防御，以防止提示注入攻击试图迫使代理偏离用户的指令。 在自动模式下运行时，探针会扫描工具结果以查找潜在的恶意指令，并且自动模式会检查操作是否与用户意图一致。 我们测试了自动模式与无防护模式的比较，以说明这种纵深防御方法的强大功能。

我们委托第三方 Trajectory Labs 进行了评估，该实验室在截至 2026 年 7 月 17 日的最新公开版本的 Claude Code 和 Codex 中测试了不同的模型。他们测试了 Anthropic 提供的 72 个间接提示注入场景。 每个场景都测试了 10 次。 在非测试环境中，成功的攻击将导致不可逆转的行为，从而损害用户，例如敏感数据泄露、财务欺诈或凭证网络钓鱼。 这些攻击针对 Claude Opus 4.7 进行了优化，而 Claude Opus 4.7 不在报告的集合中，因此评估中的每个模型都将它们视为看不见的攻击。 除了自动模式之外，评估还考察了 Claude Code 的绕过权限模式和 Codex 的完全访问模式。

Codex 和 Claude Code 均使用由 Trajectory Labs, PBC 制作的相同浏览器集成进行评估。 此集成提供了一组 MCP 工具，它们是常见 Chrome API（例如“navigate”）的精简包装。 第一方浏览器集成中内置的保护措施（例如 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 提供的 Chrome 扩展）尚未经过测试。 因此，这些结果应被视为对底层模型的测量，而不是给定部署中可能存在的完整防护措施集。

在此评估中，针对运行自动模式的 Claude Fable 5、Opus 5 或 Sonnet 5 的 720 次攻击尝试均未成功。 另一方面，针对运行 Codex 自动审查模式的 GPT-5.6 Sol 的攻击有 5.83% 成功。 值得注意的是，这高于在没有额外保护措施的情况下，针对在绕过权限模式下运行的最新模型的 0.09% 平均攻击成功率。 测试显示，在完全访问模式下运行时，针对 GPT-5.6 Sol 的攻击成功率为 19.03%。 工具以文本形式返回结果的任务和需要通过屏幕截图与浏览器交互的任务之间的攻击成功率有所不同，如下所示。

Anthropic 内部避免了三起自动模式事故

自动模式也是 Anthropic 所有 Claude Code 内部使用的默认模式。 以下是分类器在内部阻止的三个操作：

  • 网外数据泄露：当上传到内部驱动器失败时，克劳德的后备措施是将相同的报告发布到公共代码共享网站。 自动模式拒绝回退并提示用户执行后续步骤。
  • 破坏性的大规模操作：在一次长时间运行的会话中，Claude 尝试对大约 2000 个 Pod 进行大规模进程终止，并进行排队删除，这可能会导致数百个正在运行的训练作业的 GPU 崩溃。 自动模式在执行前标记破坏性命令。
  • 过于广泛的权限升级：当要求提供只读计费访问权限时，Claude 找到了一个云角色，可以在帐户根目录授予完全的管理控制权。 自动模式发现了请求的内容与授予的角色之间的不匹配。

在每种情况下，克劳德要么自己找到一条更安全的路径，要么在继续之前与用户核实。

让自动模式更安全

我们不断投资新的自动模式功能，使交付生产代码更安全、更轻松。 最近的例子包括：

  • 硬否认：数据泄露，例如将您的代码或秘密发送到外部某个地方，属于分类器设计永远不会批准的类别。 要运行这样的操作，您必须退出自动模式或自己运行命令。 硬拒绝规则可通过设置进行自定义，因此您可以添加更多您永远不想允许的规则，即使组织中的用户请求也是如此。
  • 数据访问和共享规则：分类器现在带有区分秘密和潜在敏感/机密信息的明确规则，以及每个信息可以访问和共享的位置。 为了使这些规则可执行，它还会在操作运行之前检查 git Push 或 Pull 请求的目的地是公共的、私有的还是受信任的。 同样的推送可以是例行公事，也可以是渗透，具体取决于它所在的位置：属于团队私有存储库中的代码不应最终出现在公共存储库中，并且分类器现在旨在标记何时可能发生这种情况。
  • 在破坏性 git 操作之前检查 git 状态：在可能丢弃未提交工作的命令（例如 git reset --hard）之前，分类器会查看存储库的当前 git 状态，让自动模式知道正在重置的内容。
  • 提示注入筛选：当 Claude 从外部来源（例如网页、文件内容或工具输出）提取内容时，API 端探测器会检查该内容是否试图劫持 Claude 的行为。 当某些事情看起来像是注入尝试时，在与用户共享结果之前，会在 Claude 的上下文中添加一条警告。

生产中的自动模式

团队已经将自动模式作为其生产默认模式运行：

  • Adobe 的营销平台团队负责确保 Adob​​e.com 上 90 多个国家/地区和 30 多种语言的定价和促销页面准确且最新。 他们构建了一个代理循环来构建和验证这些页面，并在自动模式下运行它，以便工程师收到完成的 PR 进行审查。
  • Nuro 在其研究和工程组织中运行自动模式，利用它为夜间研究代理提供动力，以爬山评估指标并在早上返回完成的 PR 供审查。
  • Gusto 采用自动模式来结束权限疲劳，这种疲劳迫使工程师完全绕过权限检查。 自 5 月中旬以来，大约 10% 的会话包含分类器拒绝——这证明它正在做真正的工作，而不会减慢合法任务的速度。
  • Garner Health 通过托管设置将自动模式推为所有 550 名员工的默认模式，标准化了公司范围内的软件开发生命周期 (SDLC)，不再依赖于手动管理的命令允许列表。
